item.title: Peace Corps Tonga welcomes 18 new volunteers

item.content:encoded:
A group of 18 new U.S. Peace Corps volunteers will serve in Tonga for two years following the completion of an intensive ten-week PreService Training program.

The group were sworn-in during a ceremony on Friday, 28 August, at Siva’s Café in Te’ekiu. Deputy PM Hon. Dr Viliami Latu, formally accepted the 18 new volunteers on behalf of the Tonga government, welcoming their commitment to serve communities across the Kingdom.

“Peace Corps Volunteers have served in the Kingdom of Tonga since 1968 and since then more than 1,700 Americans have served here. We are grateful to the Tongan government for their unwavering support of the Peace Corps program and our Volunteers,” said Peace Corps’ Country Director for Tonga, Elizabeth Neason.

The cohort of 18 trainees arrived in June from 13 different U.S. states, united in their commitment to serve the people of Tonga. Throughout the training period, the trainees dedicated themselves to personal growth, cultural learning, and technical preparation. Their program included approximately 150 hours of Tongan language and culture, 50 hours of health, safety, and security training, and 140 hours of specialized education, and environment sector preparation. Hosted by families in Te'ekiu, Ha'utu, and Fahefa, the trainees immersed themselves in Tongan daily life and customs, strengthening crosscultural understanding and forming strong community relationships. They also participated in practicums that placed them directly into classrooms and communities, allowing them to apply their teaching techniques and environmental education skills in realworld settings.

Seven volunteers will serve in education, teaching English language skills to primary and middle school students, collaborate with teachers, and support community literacy efforts.

Eleven trainees will serve in the environment sector, partnering with local organizations to promote environmental stewardship, strengthen naturebased resilience practices, and support disaster preparedness and risk reduction initiatives.

Peace Corps Tonga ackowledged the host families, training staff, ministry and NGO partners, and the medical and administrative teams, for their guidance and support.

The Ministers of Education, Agriculture, and Fisheries, members of the diplomatic corps, NGO s, host families, and Peace Corps staff joined the ceremony.

item.title: Tonga U-16 depart Tonga for OFC U-16 championship
item.description: Tonga’s 'Future Mataliki' Under-16 women's team have departed for Honiara to compete in the 8th OFC U-16 Women’s Championships today. The women’s team of 20 players is travelling through Fiji before continuing to the Solomon Islands.
item.content:encoded:
Tonga’s 'Future Mataliki' Under-16 women's team have departed for Honiara to compete in the 8th OFC U-16 Women’s Championships today.

The women’s team of 20 players is travelling through Fiji before continuing to the Solomon Islands.

The team will begin final preparations in Honiara ahead of its opening Group B match against Samoa on Monday.

Team Tonga will then face Papua New Guinea on September 10 before completing the group stage against New Caledonia on September 13. All three matches will be played at the Solomon Islands National Stadium.

Head coach Mark ‘Uhatahi said the team had completed several months of preparation at the Loto-Tonga Soka Centre, including training and friendly matches.

He said while the full squad had not trained together throughout the entire preparation period, the work completed in Tonga had been satisfactory.

“Once we have everyone together, we will fully complete our game plans in Solomon Islands before the games,” ‘Uhatahi said.

The squad includes returning players India May Mann, Vea Tenifa and Melia Manning, who competed at last year’s championship.

Several players also featured in Tonga’s U-15 Girls team that competed in Fiji earlier this year, including Tiulipe Tali and Langakali Peni.

Tonga finished fifth at the previous OFC U-16 Women’s Championship, ending its campaign with a 1-0 win over Fiji.

‘Uhatahi said the team was familiar with many of its regional opponents but would prepare equally for each group match.

“All games are crucial. We are preparing evenly for all three pool matches because they are all tough opponents,” he said.

He said the team’s preparations were now complete and asked for the support and prayers of Tonga as the players begin their campaign.

“The girls are prepared for battle,” ‘Uhatahi said.

The team are expected to hold their first full-squad training session in Honiara following their arrival.

item.content:encoded:
International visitors, the First Nations & Pasifika XV rugby team members, were welcomed with a traditional kava ceremony in Nuku'alofa last night, ahead of Friday’s inaugural Kaume’a Ofi Trophy match at Teufaiva Stadium.

The Tonga Rugby Union and Tonga President’s XV hosted the visiting team and staff at a function held at Ancient Tonga, bringing the two sides together in a display of culture, respect and friendship.

First Nations & Pasifika XV Manager, Matt Sonter, acknowledged the importance of the kava ceremony and Tongan traditions.

Sonter presented a gift to the Tongan leader of the ceremony, describing it as a gesture of respect rooted in his Indigenous culture.

“Where I come from, we give a gift as a sign of respect for the elders and the keepers of the land, past, present and future,” Sonter said.

He said the match carried significance beyond rugby, particularly for Australian-born players of Tongan heritage.

“I believe this is something truly special because our Tongan boys, born as Australians, are here on the shores of their ancestors for the very first time,” he said.

Australian High Commissioner to Tonga Brek Batley said the match would strengthen ties between Tonga and Australia and provide opportunities for local players to reach international rugby.

“This competition being held for the first time will bring the two nations together, strengthening rugby in the Pacific. Pacific rugby shapes global rugby,” Batley said.

Team Tonga's captain Matani Puloka said the team had prepared well and was looking forward to representing the country in front of a home crowd.

“We are excited to represent our country and our people. Whatever will happen, that is the very best that we have given,” Puloka said.

He urged supporters to attend the match, saying a full stadium would give the team confidence.

“It would give us a lot of courage to look out into a filled stadium, so Tonga, come and watch the game, cheer for us and the visiting team,” he said.

Entry to Teufaiva Stadium will be free on Friday, allowing the public to attend the first-of-its-kind fixture.

The Kaume’a Ofi Trophy match will be played at Teufaiva Stadium on Friday, bringing together players from Tonga and Australia’s First Nations and Pasifika communities in a celebration of rugby and shared Pacific heritage.

item.title: Tonga, First Nations and Pasifika squads named for inaugural Kaume’a Ofi Trophy
item.description: Tonga’s President’s XV and the First Nations & Pasifika XV have named their squads for the inaugural Kaume’a Ofi Trophy to be held at Teufaiva Stadium, this Friday 4 September 2026. The international match will bring together locally based Tongan players and a side featuring First Nations and Pasifika players from across Australian rugby.
item.content:encoded:
Tonga’s President’s XV and the First Nations & Pasifika XV have named their squads for the inaugural Kaume’a Ofi Trophy to be held at Teufaiva Stadium, this Friday 4 September 2026.

The international match will bring together locally based Tongan players and a side featuring First Nations and Pasifika players from across Australian rugby.

The Tonga President’s XV provides an opportunity for local Tongan players to represent their country in front of a home crowd, with coach Benhur Kivalu saying the match would help identify talent ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

“This is a very special opportunity for Tonga and everyone involved in the Kaume’a Ofi Trophy,” Kivalu said.

“It gives us a chance to have a look at some of our local-based players, see how they perform against quality opposition and identify the potential that is here in Tonga.”

The squad combines established domestic players with emerging talent, including players coming through Tonga’s under-20 system.

Captain Vutulongo Puloka said representing Tonga in front of family and friends would be a significant moment for the players.

“Normally, the Ikale Tahi is the team our fans see representing Tonga, so for the local boys to have the opportunity to run out and represent the country in front of our families, friends and supporters is something really special,” Puloka said.

He said the match would also give younger players a chance to see a pathway from domestic rugby to representative competition.

The fixture is also intended to promote cultural exchange between Tonga and Australia.

Puloka said the visiting players would be welcomed to Tonga and given an opportunity to experience the country’s culture and traditions.

“It is really important for us to exchange cultures and learn from each other,” he said.

“We are excited to show what Tonga is all about, especially our Anga’ofa, our friendly and loving way of life.”

The First Nations & Pasifika XV features players of First Nations, Tongan, Samoan, Fijian and Māori heritage and builds on the side’s historic appearance against the British & Irish Lions in 2025.

Former Wallaby and NSW Waratahs great Wycliff Palu will coach the side, assisted by Eddie Aholehei and Christian Leali’ifano.

Palu, who is of Tongan heritage, said the match was about more than rugby.

“This is a special opportunity for these players to represent their communities, their cultures and the people who have helped them get to where they are today,” Palu said.

“Taking this group to Tonga and being able to share in the culture, while also playing against a team of locally based Tongan players, makes this much more than just a rugby match.”

Among the selections are brothers Chace and BJ Oates, who will represent their First Nations heritage together.

BJ Oates said sharing the experience with his brother made the opportunity particularly meaningful.

“It’s about representing where we come from, our family and our community, but also embracing the opportunity to learn from the Tongan players and experience their culture,” he said.

ACT Brumbies prop Lington Leli will also bring his Fijian heritage to the touring squad.

“I’m grateful for the opportunity to represent the First Nations & Pasifika XV and also represent my Fijian heritage,” Leli said.

“Rugby is part of our Pacific culture, and it brings people from different backgrounds together.”

The Kaume’a Ofi Trophy, meaning “Close Friends” in Tongan, is supported by the Australian Government’s PacificAus Sports initiative and is being delivered in collaboration between Tonga Rugby Union and Rugby Australia.

The trophy aims to celebrate the relationship between Tonga and Australia and use rugby to strengthen cultural and community connections.

item.title: Tonga signs deal with United States to “protect critical government systems”
item.description: Prime Minister Lord Fakafanua has signed an agreement with the United States Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau to strengthen Tonga's digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, and digital transformation. item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Lord Fakafanua has signed an agreement with the United States Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau to strengthen Tonga's digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, and digital transformation. The two met yesterday, 2 September, on the margins of the 55 th Pacific Islands Forum leaders meeting in Palau.

The agreement will support a feasibility study, funded through the United States Trade and Development Agency ( USTDA ), to explore options for secure and resilient hosting of critical government systems and services, with a focus on trusted technology and strengthened digital security.

PM Lord Fakafanua said that, ”Strengthening Tonga's digital infrastructure is essential to building a more resilient, secure and connected nation. This partnership with the United States will help us protect critical government systems, strengthen cybersecurity and provide a secure foundation for expanding digital public services. It is an important investment in Tonga's digital future and in our ability to harness technology to improve services and create greater opportunities for our people."

Tonga's Digital Transformation Department has selected New York-based CyberCX USA Inc. to undertake the technical analysis required to inform the financing and potential implementation of the modernised data centre infrastructure.

The Office of the Prime Minister ( PMO ) stated that the cooperation forms part of broader efforts by the United States to support Tonga's digital resilience and promote secure and trusted digital infrastructure across the Pacific. The United States Department of State is also providing ongoing support to assist Tonga in migrating critical government data assets to trusted cloud infrastructure.

“The initiative also reflects the importance Tonga places on working with trusted international partners to strengthen national cybersecurity, protect critical government systems and ensure that the benefits of digital transformation translate into improved services and greater opportunities for the people of Tonga,” PMO stated.

item.title: Interference blamed as pullouts mar Pacific summit
item.description: Australia's Anthony Albanese, Chris Bowen and Pat Conroy will all travel to Palau on Monday for the Pacific Islands Forum leaders meeting. A third of Pacific Islands Forum leaders may miss this week's summit in a blow to regional unity that could deteriorate into a crisis.
item.content:encoded:
Australia's Anthony Albanese, Chris Bowen and Pat Conroy will all travel to Palau on Monday for the Pacific Islands Forum leaders meeting.

A third of Pacific Islands Forum leaders may miss this week's summit in a blow to regional unity that could deteriorate into a crisis.

However, Australian and New Zealand officials are downplaying the impact of the pull-outs, some of which they privately blame on Chinese pressure.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will fly out to Palau on Monday to lead Australia's delegation at the annual PIF leaders meeting.

For various reasons - domestic politics, poor health, and unspoken defiance - seven leaders may not attend.

The leaders from Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu are out, while there are conflicting reports about the participation of counterparts from Nauru and New Caledonia.

The most concerning no-shows from a regional standpoint are Kiribati and the Solomon Islands.

While other missing leaders will have deputies or foreign ministers standing in, Kiribati President Taneti Maamau is effectively snubbing the summit by sending a senior public servant - and former ambassador to China.

That decision has raised eyebrows, if not alarm bells, in Canberra given last week the Micronesian nation began the process of embedding ties to Beijing in its constitution.

Mr Maamau has blamed a difficult transit and a clash with parliament for not attending.

Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale has also offered apologies, but not before landing in Palau's capital Koror this weekend.

Mr Wale was one of a string of leaders taking advantage of New Zealand's offer to facilitate their travel on a defence force flight from Auckland and Brisbane on Saturday.

However, the recently installed prime minister left early on Sunday when one of his cabinet ministers moved a motion of no confidence in his leadership.

Home Affairs Minister Manasseh Maelanga cited Mr Wale's failure to consult on key decisions for his motion.

The threat to Mr Wale's leadership comes after the 58-year-old shifted Honiara's outlook to a more Australia-friendly stance and began negotiating a fresh treaty.

Australia holds concerns that the ructions may be tied to those talks, and possibly influenced by China.

New Zealand, too, believes the harsh hand of greater powers is at play in the pull-outs.

Foreign Minister Winston Peters said Kiribati's move was "hugely disappointing" and, asked if foreign interference was involved, didn't disagree.

" You'd be defying gravity and logic if you said it wasn't a big problem," he told journalists in Palau.

Officials on both sides of the Tasman point out it is not the first time that PIF summits have missed leaders but insist the show goes on.

" The centrality of the Pacific Islands Forum is not going to be compromised ... but it doesn't help," Mr Peters continued.

Mr Peters is on duty for Prime Minister Chris Luxon, who arrives two days after Mr Albanese, as the pair of Kiwi politicians navigate an election on November 7.

Organisers expect to welcome around 2000 visitors to Koror this week, including officials from Pacific nations and further beyond.

After a smaller summit last year in Honiara, Palau President Surangel Whipps Jr has re-opened the occasion to other nations, with many of the world's major powers sending delegations.

Deputy Secretary of State Chris Landau will lead the US contingent, while Taiwan's Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung will also attend.

Alongside Mr Albanese, Australia's Climate Minister Chris Bowen and Pacific Minister Pat Conroy will also travel.

item.title: National Reserve Bank of Tonga maintains neutral stance while strengthening monetary policy transmission
item.description: Policy Decision: The National Reserve Bank of Tonga ( NRBT ) Board of Directors has approved “maintaining a neutral monetary policy stance for the next six months”. The monetary policy rate will remain at 2 percent, the interest rate corridor will be maintained at 0 – 4 percent, and the Statutory Reserve Deposit rate will remain unchanged at 15 percent.
item.content:encoded:
Policy Decision: The National Reserve Bank of Tonga ( NRBT ) Board of Directors has approved “maintaining a neutral monetary policy stance for the next six months”.

The monetary policy rate will remain at 2 percent, the interest rate corridor will be maintained at 0 – 4 percent, and the Statutory Reserve Deposit rate will remain unchanged at 15 percent.

Headline inflation increased to 9.3% in July 2026, well above the NRBT 5% reference rate and highest since January 2024. This increase is adding to costs of living for households and raising costs for businesses, placing further strain on already constrained budgets. Inflation has been driven mainly by external supply-side shocks and, while elevated, remains below the higher level projected for second half of 2026.

Governor Moeaki stated that “domestic demand pressures appear contained, foreign reserves adequate, the financial system remains stable. At the same time, NRBT continues to strengthen monetary policy transmission as part of its broader modernization so that monetary policy can more effectively influence liquidity, interest rates, credit conditions and ultimately inflation.”

The stance will remain data-dependent where NRBT stands ready to adjust monetary policy if demand-side inflationary pressures, or second-round effects intensify. To guide its assessment, NRBT will closely monitor core inflation and second-round effects, domestic credit and liquidity conditions, foreign reserve adequacy and exchange-rate pressures, remittance and imported-price developments, and progress in absorbing excess liquidity through NRBT Notes.

Electronic copy of the MPS is available from our website www.reservebank.to
